# Get-ZbxTriggerPrototype

## SYNOPSIS

Gets the trigger prototypes that discovery rules turn into triggers.

## SYNTAX

## DESCRIPTION

A trigger prototype is the pattern a discovery rule turns into one trigger per entity it finds. The Get-ZbxTriggerPrototype cmdlet reads them with triggerprototype.get: all of them up to -Limit, by name with -Name (* and ? are wildcards), by id with -Id or from the pipeline, or with the whole triggerprototype.get selection in -Filter. -Group, -Template, -Host and the other object filters narrow the result to the trigger prototypes of the objects given, each a name, an id or a piped object. It writes ZabbixTriggerPrototype objects, with their related objects when a -Select switch asks for them, or, with -CountOutput, the number of matches; it needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Get a trigger prototype by name

```powershell
Get-ZbxTriggerPrototype -Name 'Free space is low on {#FSNAME}'
```

Gets the trigger prototype named Free space is low on {#FSNAME}. A * or ? in -Name makes it a search, so -Name 'Free*' gets every trigger prototype whose name starts with Free.

### Example 2: Get the trigger prototypes of a host

```powershell
Get-ZbxTriggerPrototype -Host 'web-01'
```

Gets the trigger prototypes of the host web-01. -Host takes a name, an id or an object; a host piped from Get-ZbxHost binds to it by its HostId property.

### Example 3: Search trigger prototypes with a filter

```powershell
Get-ZbxTriggerPrototype -Filter @{ search = @{ description = 'Free' }; limit = 10 }
```

-Filter takes the whole triggerprototype.get selection, keyed by the API's field names: here at most ten trigger prototypes whose description contains Free.
